On the hypothesis that the lattice defects (interstitial atoms or vacant sites), introduced by departure from stoichiometric composition, interact with one another when in adjacent lattice positions, the problem reduces to a form similar to that of Fowler’s treatment of regular localized monolayers. It follows that below a certain temperature, determined by the energy of interaction of lattice defects, the phase is stable only when the concentration of defects is less than some limiting value. If this is exceeded, the phase breaks up into a two-phase system. Hence the range of existence of any compound is limited on either side by the compositions at which, for example, the concentration of vacant cation sites and of interstitial atoms reach limiting values. The dependence of these limits on the partial pressure of the volatile component and the degree of lattice disorder in the stoichiometric phase is worked out. The conditions emerge under which (a) the stoichiometric compound may be metastable (e.g. FeS) and (b) the phase is incapable of existence. Experimental pressure-composition isotherms for the systems Pt-PtS-PtS2, MS-MS2 (M = Fe, Co or Ni), and UO3-U3O8 are compared with the model. The general form of the equilibrium diagrams is satisfactorily reproduced, and the limitations of the model are shown. The formation of anomalous solid solutions between compounds of different formula type (e.g. YF3 and CaF2) is finally discussed and shown to fall within the scope of the theory.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1946.0005\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[1946, 1, 10]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.70675…

Decomposition-Indexed Classicality: An A/R/F Framework for Observer-Dependent Quantum Experience
Authors/Creators
Almon, Ricardo
(Producer)

Producer:
Almon, Ricardo
Description
This work develops a quantitative framework for
observer-dependent classicality
in quantum mechanics based on three operational functionals:
Redundancy (R)
,
Accessibility (A)
, and
Observer Flow (F)
. The A/R/F framework distinguishes environmental redundancy from the effective redundancy usable by a specific observer, models accessibility through a noisy-threshold aperture function, and introduces a continuity measure governing an observer’s capacity to integrate records over time. Classicality becomes a
decomposition-indexed property
, not a global feature of the universal wavefunction.
Applied to
Wigner’s Friend
and
Frauchiger–Renner
, the framework dissolves paradoxes by showing that cross-agent inferences fail precisely in regimes where effective accessibility is low. The paper outlines experimental signatures, including observer-dependent classicality thresholds and flow-disruption tests, offering a route toward
empirical constraints on observer-relative quantum structure
.
